title: Data use & inference liability — scratchpad
content:
Purpose: quick personal notes to use during counterparty negotiations for clauses that touch customer data, model outputs, and inference-related liability. Informal — lots of open questions + suggested fallback language.

Context notes (short):
- Redwood offers Hosted API, Dedicated pools, and Private deployments. Negotiation posture changes by deployment: hosted = limit logs + strong SLA commercial terms; dedicated/private = more customer control, but still need to protect platform from unlimited downstream liability.
- Key risk vectors: PII in prompts, customer-supplied models/weights, hallucinated outputs causing third-party harm, regulatory data residency, audit rights, export controls.

Clauses to watch (high level):
1) Inference output liability / downstream harms — HIGH
   - Opposing language often tries to make vendor responsible for customer app outputs.
   - Suggested pushback: vendor provides models and runtime 'as-is'; carve-out for willful misconduct and gross negligence only; otherwise indemnity capped.
   - Suggested redline snippet: 'Vendor shall not be liable for losses arising solely from Customer's use of model outputs in production, except to the extent caused by Vendor's gross negligence or willful misconduct.'
   - Negotiation script: 'We can't accept open-ended responsibility for how customers use generated outputs. We operate the platform and provide the model runtime; the customer controls prompts and integration.'

2) Data use & retention / training on customer prompts — HIGH
   - Watch for language that allows vendor to use customer prompts to train models without restriction.
   - Desired: explicit no-training-on-customer-data for hosted by default; acceptable to offer opt-in (commercial add-on) or allow aggregated, anonymized telemetry only.
   - Snippet: 'Vendor will not use Customer-provided prompts, completion text, or other Customer Data to train or improve models used for third parties without Customer's prior written consent.'
   - Script: 'We can provide telemetry to improve the service but only with explicit opt-in. If training is required, we need an addendum and stronger data protections.'

3) Audit rights & security assessments — MED
   - Customers ask for on-site audits or full access. For hosted, push for SOC2 reports + penetration test summaries instead of full audits. For Private, limited inspection and redacted logs ok.
   - Snippet: 'Vendor will provide latest SOC2 Type II report and a summary of third-party penetration testing upon request; on-site audits may be considered under a paid professional services arrangement.'

4) Indemnity caps & carve-outs — HIGH
   - Counterparties may want uncapped indemnity for IP and data. We should: cap aggregate liability to committed fees (or a multiple) and carve consumer harms carefully.
   - Snippet: 'Vendor's aggregate liability arising from this agreement shall not exceed the greater of (i) the amount of fees paid by Customer in the 12 months preceding the claim or (ii) $1,000,000.' (numbers placeholder — business must confirm)

5) Export controls & sanctions screening — LOW/MED
   - Ensure ability to block usage from sanctioned regions and comply with export laws.

6) Subprocessors / subcontracting — MED
   - For hosted: list major cloud providers as subprocessors; commit to notify of material changes. For private: customers run their infra so fewer concerns.

Edge-case topics to flag during calls:
- Customer wants right to 'retrain' vendor model with their data and then own resulting model weights — clarify IP/ownership, proposed: customer can get an exported model only under a separate 'model-export' agreement with pricing and security constraints.
- Requests for 'delete all logs' within 24 hours — fine for some logs, but KV cache / persistent telemetry may need explicit retention policy; propose 30 days standard with negotiated shorter retention for premium contract.

Negotiation playbook (quick):
- Opening: confirm deployment type + data flow (who controls keys, where data stored).
- If customer presses on training use: offer opt-in program + price premium or allow anonymized telemetry only.
- If customer insists on broad indemnities: ask for reciprocal indemnities and insist on monetary cap tied to fees.
- Escalation trigger to Legal Director: customer asks for uncapped indemnity OR on-site source-code inspection OR ability to export core models without controls.

Fallback positions (ordered):
1) Agree with commercial add-ons for training/use & model export + security attestation.
2) If no add-on allowed, agree to deletion/retention terms and strong data segregation commitments.
3) Walk-away if customer demands unlimited indemnity or source-code escrow + public disclosure requirements.

Sample negotiation lines (short, usable):
- 'We run the runtime and provide model packages; downstream application logic is under your control, so liability for user-facing outputs should remain with the integrator.'
- 'We're happy to offer a training program, but it requires a different commercial and security model — let's scope that as an addendum.'
- 'For hosted customers, our SOC2 Type II report and redacted pentest summaries are available — full on-site code audits are not part of the standard offering.'

Open questions / TODOs: (for call prep)
- Confirm commercial cap number with finance (placeholder $1M above is illustrative).
- Get updated list of subprocessors and retention periods from infra team. (ask Ethan)
- Draft a short addendum template for 'training opt-in' that covers security, deletion, and pricing.
- Check with product about technical feasibility of 'no-training' enforcement for hosted models (prompt telemetry block).

Quick risk matrix (subjective):
- Training on customer data without consent: HIGH (reputational + regulatory)
- Unlimited inference-output indemnity: HIGH (financial exposure)
- On-site source review demands: MED-HIGH (IP leakage risk)
- Short retention + deletion demands under 24 hours: MED (operational feasibility)

Notes to self: keep language terse during redlines, don't concede 'training' language as a given, loop in product + infra early. Tag any contract that touches 'model export' for executive review.

References / scripts to paste in live redline: (use single-line copies)
- No-training: 'Vendor shall not use Customer Data to train, tune, or improve any models used to serve other customers, without Customer's prior written consent.'
- Liability carve: 'Except for liability resulting from Vendor's gross negligence or willful misconduct, Vendor's liability arising out of this Agreement will be limited to the amount set forth in the Agreement.'

End scratchpad — lightweight, shareable, intended for negotiating calls and pre-meeting prep. Keep copy in personal drive until formalized into a playbook.
